deep.reconstruction:
Context: a draft (1953) treating Schatten–von Neumann classes of compact ('complètement continus') operators on Hilbert space. S_p(A) = ||A||_p = (Σ s_i(A)^p)^{1/p}, with s_i(A) the singular values, also for 0<p<1. The previous page proves monotonicity/comparison inequalities and begins a crossed-out proof of formula (6), the Hölder inequality S_r(AB) ≤ S_p(A) S_q(B) for 1/p+1/q ≥ 1/r. That attempt went through a Carleman/Fredholm-type integral representation of S_r by ∫ log M(ρ) ρ^{-1-r} dρ. On this page Grothendieck abandons that route for the hardest formula (6) and announces a 'direct and very simple' proof in the case p,q ≥ 1, r = 1, i.e. ordinary trace-class Hölder. He notes the proof works verbatim for a normal trace σ on a weakly closed self-adjoint operator algebra (a von Neumann algebra with a normal trace), where L^p consists of A with σ(|A|^p) < ∞.

The key lemma (11): for compact A_1,…,A_{2^n}, ||A_1⋯A_{2^n}||_1 ≤ Π ||A_i||_{2^n}. The proof is by induction on n.
- Base case n=1: the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality |Tr(XY)| ≤ ||X||_2 ||Y||_2, more precisely ||XY||_1 ≤ ||X||_2||Y||_2.
- Inductive step: group the factors in pairs. The induction hypothesis bounds the product by Π ||A_{2j-1}A_{2j}||_{2^{n-1}}, which reduces everything to ||AB||_{2^{n-1}} ≤ ||A||_{2^n}||B||_{2^n}.
- Next page: ||AB||_{2^{n-1}}^{2^{n-1}} = Tr C with C = (ABB*A*)^{2^{n-2}} ≥ 0. By cyclicity Tr C = Tr C' with C' = (A*A·BB*)^{2^{n-2}}, a product of 2^{n-1} factors.
- Then |Tr C'| ≤ ||C'||_1 ≤ (||A*A||_{2^{n-1}} ||BB*||_{2^{n-1}})^{2^{n-2}} by the induction hypothesis again, and ||A*A||_{2^{n-1}} = ||A||_{2^n}^2.

Footnote (1) remarks that (11) alone suffices to derive the general Hölder inequality (6). Presumably this goes by splitting |A|, |B*| into equal fractional powers via polar decomposition, which gives dyadic exponents, then density/continuity and monotonicity of ||·||_r in r. A marginal note (partly illegible) says it suffices to treat some reduced case. The purpose is to establish the basic inequalities of Schatten classes, likely for use in the tensor-product / Fredholm-theory work of 1953–55 and its von Neumann-algebra analogue.
errors: No mathematical error in the displayed steps.
Base case n=1 is asserted without proof; the struck words '(formule ... bien [connue])' indicate Cauchy–Schwarz for Hilbert–Schmidt operators.

Cyclicity Tr(XY)=Tr(YX) is used tacitly. For compact operators this is fine since the relevant products are trace class. For a general normal trace on a von Neumann algebra it needs justification (e.g. Dixmier 1953), which is not given here.
The reduction from (11) to general exponents (footnote) is only announced, not carried out on this page.

ideas.what: Hölder inequality for Schatten classes, ||AB||_1 ≤ ||A||_p||B||_q, with the generalisation to 1/r ≤ 1/p+1/q
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for Schatten–von Neumann classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann, Schatten (1940s), Dunford–Schwartz; Horn/Weyl singular value inequalities
ideas.where_published: Possibly used in Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955) and in the Bourbaki seminar exposé on rearrangements and convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras with a trace (1955); unsure of exact content

ideas.what: Dyadic induction proof via ||AB||_{2^{n-1}}^{2^{n-1}} = Tr(A*A BB*)^{2^{n-2}} and cyclicity
ideas.modern_name: dyadic (power-of-two) trick / Cauchy–Schwarz iteration for trace inequalities
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; similar arguments in Dixmier (1953) and in proofs of generalized Hölder

ideas.what: Extension to a normal trace on a von Neumann algebra (non-commutative L^p)
ideas.modern_name: non-commutative L^p spaces / Hölder for semifinite normal traces
ideas.where_published: Probably the Séminaire Bourbaki exposé on rearrangement inequalities in von Neumann algebras with trace (1955)

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard proof of trace-class Hölder by dyadic induction, with the remark that it carries over to normal traces on von Neumann algebras. This was contemporaneous with and covered by Segal and Dixmier (1953). It is mildly interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's involvement with non-commutative integration, which surfaced in his 1955 Bourbaki talk, but there is nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'p ≥ 1, q ≥ 1, r = 1' is correct. The struck line beneath reads roughly 'p, q, r ≥ 1/...' with an asterisk referring to the margin note.
'd'une trace [?] ... normale [?] définie' is likely 'd'une trace normale σ définie sur une algèbre autoadjointe 𝒜 faiblement fermée'.

Footnote marker (1) text is likely 'les "opérateurs de puissance p-ième sommable [pour la trace σ]" de 𝒜 se définissant comme ceux A ∈ 𝒜 tels que σ(|A|^p) < +∞', with the symbol before (|A|^p) being σ.
'on démontré pour 2^{n-1} facteurs' is better read 'supposé démontré pour 2^{n-1} facteurs'.
The last displayed index should be ||A_{2^n-1}A_{2^n}||_{2^{n-1}}.
